author_messages.text: I’ll inspect the compiler, scoping tests, and project instructions first, then trace both static and dynamic class generation paths before editing. I’ll add a focused regression for class-based scoping, run it separately from preservation checks, and review the final diff.

The scoping marker is currently emitted in four places: selector rewriting uses `[id]`, DOM/SSR static HTML emit an attribute, and runtime hydration calls `encapsulateStyles` to add it. Dynamic `class` is handled by the generic attribute renderer, so the change must preserve the scope token when that renderer updates `className`. I’m checking runtime helpers and sample expectations now to identify the smallest compatible hook.

The required observable change is compiler output, not merely internal metadata: scoped selectors must become `.svelte-*`, rendered elements must carry that class in DOM and SSR, and a later dynamic `class` update must retain it. Existing CSS fixtures assert the old public output, while the runtime harness can verify the state transition after `component.set`; I’ll establish the baseline targeted suite before editing so the new regression is demonstrably sensitive to the old behavior.

The baseline targeted checks pass all existing CSS, runtime, SSR, and parser scoping scenarios; the only failure is the pre-existing Nightmare custom-element timeout. I’m adding a runtime regression that captures the actual rendered element before and after `component.set`, because a compile-only assertion would not prove the scope class survives a real dynamic class update.

The regression fails on the baseline exactly where expected: the rendered paragraph has the old `svelte-*` attribute, so no scope class is found, and the generated update would overwrite any manually added class marker. I’ll now switch selector rewriting and HTML emission to class selectors, add the marker through `classList` when no class attribute exists, and prefix static/dynamic `className` assignments when one does.

The production change is in place. One implementation detail is intentionally split: elements without a user `class` get the scope via the existing hydration hook, while elements with `class` receive the scope in both initial and update assignments so updates cannot erase it. I also corrected the optimized static HTML path to merge the scope and user class into one attribute rather than emitting duplicate `class` attributes.

All CSS compiler fixtures now pass the new selector and DOM/SSR HTML expectations. The remaining repository assertions are generated snapshots for JS bundles, SSR fixtures, and sourcemaps that embed the old marker form; I’m updating those through their existing test-generation paths, then I’ll run the preservation suites separately.

The class-based CSS suite passes all 52 targeted cases, including selector forms, cascade behavior, refs, static classes, dynamic classes, DOM, and SSR comparisons. I renamed the internal marker state to reflect its new meaning; before final verification I’m regenerating the two JS snapshots and sourcemap fixtures that encode compiler output, then I’ll rerun the focused regression and preservation suites from the final source.

The generated output revealed one expected snapshot detail: bundle tests also retain helper functions that are now unused, so those stale `setAttribute` helper blocks were removed from the two affected expected bundles. Sourcemap tests regenerate successfully with class selectors and className initialization. I’m now running the final focused dynamic transition check, followed by independent preservation checks for CSS, SSR, JS snapshots, sourcemaps, and lint.

content.text: Final focused checks are green: the new runtime scenario passes shared, hydration, and inline-helper modes; CSS has 52 passing cases; the SSR-inclusive preservation run has 340 passes and 10 expected pending; JS snapshots have 33 passes; sourcemaps have 8 passes; lint has no errors, only the repository’s existing ignored-file warnings. I’m running the complete project test command once to catch cross-suite regressions, then I’ll inspect status and diff scope.
